title: A New Yorker shares footage of a ghost caught on camera at his brewery, and he claims it has a 'creepy set of teeth and two eyes'
content:
Image by stevepb on Pixabay.

Category:

The owner analyzed the video.

Brenn Allen Flores

|

Published: Oct 18, 2026 02:30 pm

A brewery owner in Newburgh, New York, believes security footage from his kitchen may show something he cannot explain. Paul Halayko, who runs Newburgh Brewing Company, shared recordings showing a pale shape that he says resembles a face, along with flashes of light and apparent changes in the positions of items inside the building.

Halayko discussed the footage with News 12 Hudson Valley, pointing to a shape that appeared to have eyes and a mouth. “Kind of like a grimaced mouth right here,” he said. “Very creepy with the teeth, definitely see two eyes.”

The recordings came from a motion-activated security camera, which has always been the best tool to pick up paranormal activity, Halayko installed in February 2024. Two other clips reportedly show brief flashes of light about 47 minutes apart during the night, when the brewery was empty. Halayko said he compared the images and noticed that several kitchen items appeared to be in different places, although the recordings did not show anything moving.

Strange Things Were Going On

Among the items he identified were pots, a garbage pail and a tray. He also noticed that two knives appeared to be missing from a knife rack in the images. The footage has not established what caused the changes, and there is no independent evidence confirming that the recordings show paranormal activity.

The building’s history has added another question to the story. The brewery stands in a structure dating to the 1850s that once housed industrial businesses, including a steam engine operation and a yarn factory, before becoming the Newburgh Paper Box Company. The site later became home to Newburgh Brewing Company, which operates its brewing area downstairs and serves customers upstairs.

Halayko asked the city’s historian to look into the building’s past, hoping to learn whether a fatal accident might explain the reports. The historian found no documented fatal accidents at the property but noted that industrial work in earlier decades could be dangerous and that not every incident was necessarily recorded. The available historical information does not link any past event to the images captured by the camera.

The reports are not limited to the kitchen footage. Halayko said one employee has described seeing a man wearing overalls in the downstairs production area on several occasions. The worker reportedly viewed the encounters as harmless, like the one a TikToker had earlier this year.

The brewery has also shared images from the camera on social media, inviting people to look at the shape and decide what they see. Some viewers may interpret the pale area as a face, while others may see an ordinary shape created by lighting, shadows or the camera’s view. The images alone do not establish that a ghost was present, and the recordings do not show the kitchen items moving.

Halayko said he has not found an explanation for what appears in the footage, but he is open to the possibility that there are things people cannot explain. “I’d be crazy to say it’s not possible,” he said, “because there are many things in this world that we don’t understand.”
